Go on Mission (Optional) 5.2 End of Turn 6 Special Mechanics 6.1 Bad Buzz 6.2 Shock Tokens 7 Mission Types 8 Super Powers 8.1 Immediate Powers (♦) 8.2 Permanent Powers (◆) 8.3 Support Powers 9 Game End 10 Key Strategy Elements 11 FAQ 12 Notes Overview SUPER is a competitive card game where players manage superhero agencies, racing to reach 50 million followers by recruiting Supers and completing missions. Game Goal Be the first to reach or exceed 50 million followers by successfully completing missions with your recruited Supers. Components 4 Agency boards (6 slots each for Super cards) 56 Super cards (4 factions: blue, purple, red, green) 42 Mission cards (5 types: blue, purple, red, green, gold) Score dials, player aids, shock tokens, first player token Setup Each player gets an Agency board, player aid, and score dial (set to 00) Place 4 Super cards face-up in recruitment line Place 4 Mission cards face-up in mission line Last person to read a comic book goes first Turn Structure Each turn has two phases: Actions Phase A. Play a Super (Mandatory) Choose one of the 4 face-up Supers from recruitment line Place it on any slot in your Agency (can replace existing Supers) Apply any immediate powers First turn only : Each player must play 2 Supers B. Go on Mission (Optional) Can be done multiple times per turn Requirements : - Strength : Combined strength of sent Supers must equal/exceed mission requirement - Leader : At least one Super must match the mission's color (your choice for Rescue missions) If you send 2+ Supers of the same faction, you gain an additional Partner Bonus Used Supers are discarded after mission End of Turn Refill empty slots with new Super and Mission cards If Super deck is empty, shuffle discard pile Special Mechanics Bad Buzz Once per turn, before playing a Super, pay 2 million followers to discard all 4 face-up Supers and reveal 4 new ones. Shock Tokens Can disable opponent Supers' powers (they keep faction but lose strength/abilities). Mission Types Mission Type Effect Villain Attack Gain immediate followers Chemical Hazard Apply shock effects Destruction Threat Gain followers based on completed Destruction missions Alien Invasion Recruitment effects and ongoing faction bonuses Rescue Mission Gain followers based on variety of completed mission types Super Powers Immediate Powers (♦) Popular : Gain X followers immediately Recruitment : Draw and place a Super from deck immediately Permanent Powers (◆) Veteran : Can return to bottom row instead of being discarded after missions Shapeshifter : Counts as all factions simultaneously Strategist : 1 discount on all mission types Partner : Triggers partner bonus even without same-faction allies Power Up : Gains +X strength for each specified faction Super in your agency Influential : Gain followers when specified faction Supers are placed Ready to Go : Gain followers when specified faction Supers go on missions Support Powers Faction Support : Makes another Super count as additional faction Strength Support : Gives another Super +X strength Game End The game ends when: A player reaches 50+ million followers (finish the round), OR Mission line can't be fully refilled Winner : Player with most followers (ties are shared victories) Key Strategy Elements Balance immediate

[Rating: 3/10] Combo card game that has engine building and destruction elements (you sacrifice your engine to score points). It was ok. My opponent took forever to make their moves which is not what I'm looking for in a quick 2p card game (my own turns comprised about 20% of the game time).

[Rating: 5/10] The game feels like it is missing something.  The superhero theme is fine, but the heroes themselves have no character or personality.  I enjoy building the combos, but the shock mechanism can ruin plans and really never feels like much fun.  Also, if the right missions do not come out, there is really nothing you can do - I wish there were a bit more churn there.  I don't hate the game, but ultimately it is not anything particularly super.

[Rating: 5/10] Wasn't excited about it. Cards don't often align to get you missions and rarely did a hero effect help. No engine building really gets sustained.

[Rating: 6/10] Goupy games always make my head spin, and this is no exception. This games fits in the "falling apart engine" category of games where you are turning in pats of your engine to score and then making new engines in a sort of rolling fashion, trying to keep your favorite pieces in tact all the while. It's all very abstracted though. A lot of it is about card placement in the grid and synergies with location. It's pleasant and seems like it's on the better side of Goupy's catalog. Replay value seems high.
